thread:
maria: Heads-up — since the cert rotator ran in eu-west-1 (10:12UTC) we're seeing a brief spike in TLS handshake latencies (~200-400ms extra) and a small number of failed handshakes. KMS unwraps in the logs show a lot of throttling. anyone familiar with keystore entropy/unlock interactions?
ajay: yep saw the alert. KMS returns 429s around the rotation window. Looks like multiple services tried to unwrap the same new key at once. Not classic entropy but parallel unwrap storm.
kevin: can you paste the exact KMS error? also which keystore (proxy-keystore vs edge-keystore)?
maria: error snippet: 
```
2026-02-12T10:12:47Z WARN proxy-keystore unwrap failed status=429 KMSThrottle RetryAfter=1s request_id=abc123
2026-02-12T10:12:48Z ERROR edge-proxy tls handshake failed: tls: unexpected message
```
We use proxy-keystore for ingress and edge-keystore for egress. This was proxy-keystore most impacted.
lena: fwiw, audit logs show a burst of unwrap requests from ~50 distinct pods within 30s. rotator configured to write new key and then signal via configmap; all pods reload at once.
kevin: that matches. If every replica reloads and attempts unwrap simultaneously, KMS rate limits. We should add jitter/backoff to rotator signal or make unwrap happen lazily per first request (lazy init).
oncall-sre: rolling back the rotator isn't ideal mid-rotation. Short-term mitigation we can do: 1) increase per-account KMS throttle quota (cloud ticket), 2) throttle client-side unwrap concurrency (circuit-breaker), 3) put in a short canary window so only a subset unwraps immediately.
maria: agree. Which of those is fastest to ship?
ajay: easiest immediate: add exponential backoff with jitter in the unwrap path and treat 429 as retriable with small sleep. Patch should be tiny. Medium: add a leader-election step to rotator so only leader writes configmap and signals gradually. Long-term: KMS quota bump + keystore caching at proxy layer.
kevin: I'm worried about audit completeness. If unwraps are retried, will audit logs duplicate entries and confuse incidents? We should include an unwrap_id and retry_count in audits so we can collapse retries.
lena: good call. Our current audit schema has fields: principal, key_id, action, result, timestamp. Let's add unwrap_attempt and correlation_id when we deploy the retry. Minimal change: correlation_id = rotation_id + pod_id, unwrap_attempt as integer.
security-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-042 (mtls-unwrap-throttle-eu-west). Severity: P2. Assigned to: eng-security oncall.
oncall-sre: putting the immediate patch (client-side backoff + audit correlation_id) into a hotfix branch. Can we canary to 10% replicas in eu-west?
maria: yes please. Also we need to check for any services that did permanent TLS failures (not just transient). cc @kevin for support logs.
kevin: digging through s3 logs — found ~12 handshakes that failed and never retried (client gave up after 3 attempts). Those are mostly older Java clients with no retry heuristics. We should add server-side graceful fallback: if unwrap fails on reload, keep previous cert in memory for X minutes before evicting so clients have chance to reconnect.
ajay: server-side fallback + client backoff + audit changes sounds like the proper plan. For rollout: 1) hotfix backoff + audit fields (canary 10% now), 2) server fallback window (small change) canary 25% tomorrow, 3) quorum/leader rotator improvements next week, 4) quota ticket to cloud.
lena: also add observability: metric for unwrap_retries and unwrap_failures, and an alert when unwrap_429_rate > 0.5% in a 5m window.
maria: I'll open a tracking ticket and timeline. action items: Maria - create INC ticket and rollout plan; Ajay - open PR for client backoff + audit fields; Kevin - patch server fallback; Lena - dashboard/alerts; Oncall - monitor canary.
oncall-sre: acknowledged, will watch and be ready to roll back.
kevin: one more thought — rotation signal via configmap causes thundering herd. Could use a queue (kafka/sqs) or leader-based gradual annotation. Let's track as follow-up.
maria: thanks team. I'll post updates in this thread when canary starts. :thumbsup:
